# NOTES (compacted; use instead of source text)

## BOOK 1: THE LONG ARM OF THE MOUNTED
Author: James French Dorrance (author of "Never Fire First"). Pub. Macaulay Co., NY, 1926. Gutenberg #73900. Dedicated to Esther Dorrance, "our beloved aunt and substitute mother." Frontispiece by Edward C. Caswell (missing from source). Chapters I–XXV: I Across Medicine Line; II Rescue Unwelcome; III In the Wrong Party; IV Riding Boot Rivals; V Too Much Luck; VI Sealed Lips; VII Last Warning; VIII Threat of Doubt; IX Bust 'em, Broncho; X Home of Flame; XI Did He Dare?; XII By Single Strand; XIII In Punishment Gulch; XIV His Biggest Debt; XV Trapping for Proof; XVI Clean as a Hound's Tooth; XVII Calling a Bluff; XVIII Rustled to a Finish; XIX Surprises for Flame; XX Poor Branded Man; XXI The Nest of the Crow; XXII Threat of Spikes; XXIII Coming a Cropper; XXIV Out of the Nest; XXV Grip of the Law.

### Characters
- **Sgt. John "Jack" Childress**, Royal Canadian Mounted Police ("the Force," "Mountie"). Tall, hard-boiled, WWI vet (honor ribbons), 5 yrs Arctic patrol, Regina boxing; uses mufti (civilian clothes) undercover. Whimsical one-cornered smile. Horse **Silver**, silver-gray stallion (shoulder brand). Dog **Poison**, brindle battle-scarred hound (bought/followed him, "a white man's hound"). Sign-off "watch his step." Says he never fires first, only last.
- **Bernice "Flame" Gallegher**, of Lazy G (own brand Circle G). Red-gold braided hair, freckles across nose, big brown eyes, dimple. Wears boy clothes at first. Nicknames: "Flame of Fire Weed," "Firecracker," "Fireworks."
- **Sam Gallegher**, her father, Lazy G owner; bald, aquiline, tall, lean, dark; cuts own hair with patent clipper; bad leg from being thrown by horse; clay pipe; "Hell's tinklers."
- **Ethel Andress**, widow, owner of Rafter A ranch (brand: A with half-diamond/peaked roof). Raven hair, turquoise eyes. Husband Cliff Andress killed in Flanders. Horses: **Princess** (sorrel thoroughbred), **Blackandwhite** (piebald cow-pony, "cayuse").
- **Thomas "Tom" Fitzrapp**, manager of Rafter A/Fire Weed Ranch. Florid, aquiline nose, short sandy mustache, red scar on left cheek, flat-brimmed felt hat holed by bullet; Sandhurst grad; avoided war service; jealous suitor of Ethel. Stallion **Canada** (black thoroughbred).
- **Major Ivan MacDonald**, Ethel's uncle, pioneer, pointed gray beard, bay gelding, sportsman; knee sprain from "squeezing Lizzie" (horse).
- **Duncan "Dunc" O'Hara**, head buster; pipe; later Rafter range boss; was saved by Childress from lynch mob at end of steel (Trans-Continental railroad). Betrays Fitzrapp, steals Canada + two-year-olds.
- **Padraic "Paddy" Mahaffy**, Irish constable, rubicund, red mustache, graying; Childress's aide in ranch-hand guise.
- **Season's Greetings**, half-breed wrangler; one useless eye; arrived Christmas Eve; bullet-torn coat sleeve. **Darned Cuss**, home guard/nurse of orphan colts; wife Mrs. Cuss (housekeeper).
- **"Smiling Dick" Murdock**, Lazy G range boss, dark, swarthy; desires Flame. **Rust** (florid, drooping mustache, "Rusty") and **Roper** (ruddy youth) — punchers, brand-blotters. **Chan Toy**, Chinese cook; idolizes Flame; Rust once ringed Buddha idol with hat.
- **Commissioner Jim Maltby**, RCMP commissioner in Ottawa, Childress's old friend.
- **Doc Chase**, outguard rancher at Crow's Nest gulch; flag (white = friend); son **Tommie**.
- **Bart Crowe**, proprietor of Crow's Nest (dropped "e"); **Delores Doleroso**, dance-hall woman; **Sven Larsen**, Swedish logger (jealous, calks Childress); pegleg crook; pasty-faced violinist.
- **Sheriff of Bison County**, Montana (friend who posted Childress's wanted poster).

### Places
Medicine Line (US–Canada border; whitewashed stone monuments; Childress's "dead-line"). Soda Springs. Whitefoot Reservation. Strathconna (provincial city; King & Prince Streets; Chateau Royal hotel; Maple Leaf Midland Railroad office; Hudson's Bay post at Rowdy River/Placid fork; Victoria Park; Strathconna Hunt Club; exposition track). Fire Weed country (fireweed = snakeweed; grows 10 in., yellow flowers, burns). Witch River. Open A ranch = Childress's 640-acre railroad section in "the cup"/basin, adjoining Rafter A (east) and Gallegher (west); brand = Open A (inverted V). Friday Gulch (box canyon). Crooked Coulee, Feather Bed Meadow, Breakfast Flat, Corn Cob Basin. Crow's Nest (Bitter Root Mountains, Montana, outlaw camp). Harve, Montana (his cover address). Bitter Root lynching.

### Events, in order
1. **Ch I**: Night, Childress crosses Medicine Line on Silver with Poison. Meets girl in boy's clothes on lame bay, pursued by 5 Crow's Nest "Nesters" who charge her with horse-stealing. She faints in his arms; he tells her to swap horses, meet at Soda Springs. She refuses to flee, draws automatic. He draws a line with his heel: "a Mountie shoots, perhaps not first, but always last." Leader: "We're five to one." She: "Five to two... Come to it, you cowardly Crows!" They retreat. He calls her "Sergeant Brave but Impossible" (she calls him that). Poison.
2. **Ch II**: Next morning, Strathconna Hunt Club coyote chase on Whitefoot Reservation. Princess runs away with Ethel (broken rein). Childress rides Silver to rescue, snatches her off saddle onto Silver. She is furious ("I wanted to be in at the death"). She rides Silver to finish hunt; he ropes Princess; "Stetson's off to you."
3. **Ch III**: Childress repairs Princess's rein. Recognizes Fitzrapp (scar, aquiline nose) → Fitzrapp: "Mrs. Andress' saddler." Poison kills coyote; 35-lb coyote given to Ethel. MacDonald invites Childress to Strathconna. Childress gives name "John Childress," from Montana. MacDonald: "first masculine arm I ever approved of around her waist."
4. **Ch IV**: Ethel reflects; Fitzrapp suspects Childress as rustler chief (silver stallion seen in raids). Ethel defends him, teases Fitzrapp about "riding boot rivals."
5. **Ch V**: Strathconna described. Childress buys section at land office (one-twentieth cash; 19 annual payments; "ready-made farm"). Bernice arrives too late: "Too late!"; "Some folks have too much luck." Childress recognizes her.
6. **Ch VI**: Land-office scene; Childress offers to let her take section if he leaves; she: "I'll be damned if I'll step into any man's shoes." Fitzrapp followed Childress, reports seeing Flame. Ethel: next raid "I'm going to be in the saddle."
7. **Ch VII**: Mahaffy grumbles at Open A cabin (unroofed). Childress sends Mahaffy for supplies. Bernice rides up to Open A: "last warning" — boys plan to "eliminate" him; brand-blotting threat (Open A vs Rafter A). "Hell's bells... in my old age."
8. **Ch VIII**: Ethel rides Blackandwhite; recounts Fitzrapp's cowardice (hole in hat) and Fitzrapp sent to Strathconna horse race. She sees Childress's cabin, silver stallion; decides to warn him.
9. **Ch IX**: Childress breaks an outlaw roan in canvas corral; Ethel watches (praises him). Warns him of Fitzrapp's suspicion; he refuses to leave ("I'll stick it out"). Poison greets Ethel; "Tom Fitzrapp" said with scorn.
10. **Ch X**: Childress rides to Gallegher ranch; helps Flame pull bogged cow (her Circle G cow) out of quicksand bog with his hands. Flame smiles (dimple). Buzzards lead to skinned-alive steer in bog. Childress mercy-shoots it. "Injin stuff." Flame shoots a buzzard. They split up to track skinner ("some wandering Sioux"). Sam Gallegher notes Flame's silence.
11. **Ch XI**: Childress chases skinner across line into timber; skinner (checkerboard shirt, black felt hat) shoots at him; Childress falls into devil's-clubs, then fights brush, is trapped on ledge after skinner throws down the rung-ladder; shoots at skinner; laughter from below. He cuts down lone hemlock to make bridge across chasm ("as always... when the issue demanded he dared").
12. **Ch XII**: Crosses hemlock by hand over hand, gashes scalp; removes branch with ax (drops ax). Coin toss direction. Camps; recovers hide in gunny sack from alders. Next morning three Lazy G riders (Murdock, Roper, Rust) lasso him and Silver with sixty-foot ropes; his revolver emptied.
13. **Ch XIII**: Murdock (White Horse King accusation; cayuse with Lazy G brand). Friday Gulch trial. Plan: lashing or branding horseshoe with Lazy G on forehead with running iron (Roper's idea). Childress refuses to sign confession; asks Murdock to light his pipe; "I'll sign nothing under duress." Murdock hesitant. Flame arrives: "Rust, untie Mr. Childress instantly!"
14. **Ch XIV**: Flame's testimony (she saved him from bog; he went after skinner). Rides home with him; "call me Flame." He says he has idea ("surprise"). At Gallegher's: Ethel and Fitzrapp visiting. Joint appeal to Commissioner Ottawa signed by Ethel (Rafter A), Flame (Circle G), Sam (Lazy G), Childress (Open A). Fitzrapp challenges Childress to race Silver vs his stallion Canada at Strathconna.
15. **Ch XV**: O'Hara on colt-nursing detail (demoted by MacDonald). Reports to Fitzrapp that Ethel visited Childress in the basin. Fitzrapp jealous; resolves to trap Childress. Ethel evades his questions.
16. **Ch XVI**: Night, Poison wakes Childress. Smell of pipe tobacco; 15 unbranded two-year-olds in side ravine. Childress lassos O'Hara (who was building a rope corral). O'Hara reveals Fitzrapp's frame plan (corral Rafter horses; raid with MacDonald; "hawse-thief brand"). O'Hara asks to join; Childress says he'll return horses and wait for "clean-up." O'Hara to go back, not warn Fitzrapp.
17. **Ch XVII**: MacDonald, Fitzrapp, Cuss ride to Open A to search ravine; empty (Childress had moved horses). Race proposed: Childress challenges Fitzrapp; $1,000 each; certificate of deposit; MacDonald holds purse; race at Strathconna. MacDonald suspicious of Fitzrapp's motives.
18. **Ch XVIII**: Ethel and MacDonald on porch; Indian boy brings Fitzrapp's note ("Band of five... My love to you, Ethel"). Fitzrapp and Season's Greetings return: lost ~75 head; Fitzrapp's hat holed again. Greetings' sleeve bullet. Flashback: Ethel's visit to Open A (luncheon, trout, can-opener); she saw Flame riding with Childress.
19. **Ch XIX**: Flame finds Silver in Lazy G stable; Childress left Silver with Gallegher, went to Montana. Lazy G songs ("Roll on, little doggies"; "The Dreary, Dreary Life"). Flame sets alarm; rides east at dawn.
20. **Ch XX**: Flame meets Childress at rocky pass (Crow's Nest gap). He shows bandaged forehead: burned horseshoe scar (painted with blister paste from Strathconna). She is angry (Murdock), wants to ride with him. Flame confesses she "slipped a cinch" to wait for him. He rides on into Montana alone.
21. **Ch XXI**: Crow's Nest described (Bart Crowe, Doc Chase flag). Childress rides in; sees his own $1,000 DEAD OR ALIVE poster ("wanted for horse stealing... may wear uniform"); draws horseshoe on it; pulls it down. Delores dances with him; Sven Larsen (Swede logger) jealous.
22. **Ch XXII**: Brawl with Larsen; Larsen tries to calk him (spiked boot); Childress's gun falls out of holster; he raises forearm; calks cut to bone; Larsen falls, hits head on piano; Childress realizes he loves Flame. Crowe: "Mr. Childress is going to be my guest."
23. **Ch XXIII**: Ethel and MacDonald return from Strathconna dressmaker; Fitzrapp (left arm in sling, "came a bad cropper"); O'Hara ambushed raid with Fitzrapp, gone with Canada and 30–40 two-year-olds; Fitzrapp's account (O'Hara's jammed rifle, bowled Fitzrapp with butt). Fitzrapp produces red leather memorandum book inscribed "John Childress" as evidence. Plan: arrest Childress at race; MacDonald to offer reward for O'Hara.
24. **Ch XXIV**: Weeks at Crow's Nest; Childress makes O'Hara's acquaintance (O'Hara shares his hut). Murdock arrives at Crow's Nest. Flame arrives looking for Childress, Murdock tries to take her ("Bernie dear"); Childress shoots Murdock (fatal). Escape through window to cabin; siege; Childress wounded in shoulder; declares love ("first woman I ever said that to"). Night escape on his new horse with Flame in front.
25. **Ch XXV**: Race day, 10 a.m., Strathconna track. MacDonald, Ethel, Fitzrapp, starter, judges. Childress brings Silver and Mahaffy with cow saddle. He produces Canada (black stallion) brought by Mahaffy. Fitzrapp: "Officer, take him in charge." Warrant served; Childress reads it. Childress, Mahaffy re-appear in full RCMP parade uniform (Childress staff-sergeant). Mahaffy arrests Fitzrapp. Childress: Fitzrapp sold Canada to Dick Allen in Missoula; Childress bought it. O'Hara to be witness. Fitzrapp confesses. Childress introduces "Mrs. John Childress" (Flame, married yesterday). Ethel: "a romance of the Fire Weed." Childress to resign after case. Last words: Flame: "You better had—enjoy it!"

## BOOK 2: THE DUKE DECIDES
Author: Headon Hill (author of "By a Hair's-Breadth"). A. Wessels Co., New York, 1903/1904. Gutenberg #37413. Frontispiece: Leonie Sherman. Illustrations: "A countrywoman of yours. I wonder if you know her?"; "The procession of three led by the stranger."; "I am very far from being indifferent to Mrs. Talmage Eglinton." Chapters I–XXI: I The Man with the Mandate; II On Board the St. Paul; III A Task-master in Goggles; IV The Lady in the Landau; V Ziegler Begins to Move; VI The General is Curious; VII The Men on the Stairs; VIII The Cut Panel; IX The Strategy of the General; X A Duty Call; XI On the Terrace; XII The Man Under the Seat; XIII At the Keeper's Cottage; XIV Too Many Women; XV A New Cure for Headache; XVI A Delicate Mission; XVII Where is the Duke?; XVIII The Senator and the Securities; XIX In the Crypt; XX In the Muniment Room; XXI The Honor of the House.

### Characters
- **Charles Hanbury** (alias) = **Charles Augustus Trevor Fitzroy Hanbury, seventh Duke of Beaumanoir**. Ex-subaltern, crack English cavalry regiment, polo, gymkhana (Upper India); ruined by debt; lamed by fall down hatchway on voyage out; limps; dry-goods store drudge in New York at $8/week ($5 to boarding-house landlady; German car-driver and Irish porter neighbors; Brooklyn). Hussar-style "cavalry swing." Champion boxer, Eton. Titles: Prior's Tarrant (seat, Hertfordshire); Beaumanoir House (Piccadilly); Pattisons (family solicitors, Lincoln's Inn).
- **Jevons**: stout, fair, Cockney-accented recruiter in Bowery saloon; white Panama hat; gave $500 in five $100 notes.
- **Mr. Clinton Ziegler**: master criminal, Hotel Cecil suite on Embankment; snowy beard, purple cheeks (faked), blue/green-tinted glasses, invalid chair, parrot/piping treble voice.
- **Leopold Benzon**: Ziegler's secretary; disguised as "Colonel Anstruther Walcot, 14th Dragoon Guards" (card) — later pretends to be Mr. Ziegler's aide; sly, bold-eyed.
- **Marker**: spy in covert-coat, tweed cap, cigar in holder; shadowed Hanbury on St. Paul and into London; later under train seat.
- **Leonie Sherman**: American girl, dainty, piquant beauty, ivory complexion; loves Duke. Mother = **Mrs. Senator Sherman** (simple, admires aristocracy). Father = **Senator Leonidas Sherman** (Washington; handsome; ex-Visiting Prison Commissioner; carries 3 million pounds US Treasury bonds on the *Campania*).
- **Alec Forsyth**: Duke's Eton friend; Foreign Office third-grade clerk (£230/yr); becomes private secretary (800 a year); lodges John Street, Adelphi; engaged to Sybil. Nephew of General Sadgrove.
- **Sybil Hanbury**: Duke's orphaned cousin, 18, black-clad mourning, tomboyish, brave, slangy; living at Beaumanoir House. Father's and grandfather's background (late Duke raised her).
- **Mrs. Talmage Eglinton** = **Cora Lestrade**, American ex-convict (escaped Sing Sing), gang boss; blonde, bold eyes, childish voice; widow of Chicago (claimed); landau (coachman Bennett); also "Ziegler" in disguise; maid **Rosa** (French); scent-perfumed letters.
- **General Sadgrove** (Jem), late Indian Staff Corps, C.B., hunter of Thugs and Dacoits; gray mustache, iron visage; wife **Mrs. Sadgrove (Madge)**. Houses at 140 Grosvenor Gardens.
- **Azimoolah Khan**: Pathan orderly; black beard; cobra-hiss signal; disguised as Thakore of Bhurtnagur, as huckster, as painter-witness.
- **Servants**: Prince (butler, Beaumanoir House); William (second footman); Steptoe (first footman); Manson (butler, Prior's Tarrant); Perrett (coachman); James (footman); Mayne (gamekeeper, Sir Claude Asprey's coverts; dog Tear'em; wife; kids gone); Bristow (vicar), Mrs. Bristow (strawberries); Jennings (third gardener, lassoed).
- **Lady Roseville**: introduced Mrs. Talmage Eglinton to society.

### Places
Bowery (NY); St. Paul liner (Southampton); Waterloo; Hotel Cecil (London); Grosvenor Gardens; John Street, Adelphi; Beaumanoir House, Piccadilly; Prior's Tarrant (Hertfordshire; muniment room; crypt under Dutch garden; state bedroom with chimney); Tarrant Road station; Tarrant village; Elstree; Radlett; Kentish Town; Hendon; Mill Hill; Harpenden; St. Albans; Tring; Bletchley; Liverpool (Campania); Kettner's restaurant (Strand); Bond Street modiste; Air Street; Vienna (Cora's death); Standard (newspaper).

### Events, in order
1. **Ch I**: May evening, Bowery. Hanbury leaves store; limps; boot-store label. Jevons bumps him; drinks; offers forgery job: plant forged US Treasury bonds on Bank of England (£3 million). Threat of death for betrayal. Hanbury accepts. Telegram from Pattisons: uncle (late Duke) and cousin George Hanbury killed in railway accident (racing special to Newmarket). Hanbury now heir-duke.
2. **Ch II**: On St. Paul, day 3: Leonie Sherman ("A penny for your thoughts"). Mrs. Sherman wants English duke for daughter. Fifth day approaching Ireland: Leonie points out Marker (watching Hanbury). Marker's cabin next door.
3. **Ch III**: Southampton boat-train to Waterloo. Mrs. Sherman invites him to 140 Grosvenor Gardens. He calls on Ziegler at Cecil: masked men, chloroform threat ("Let him alone, boys"). Ziegler knows of Leonie link: Forsyth's agent placed him beside her; Senator carries bonds; call Saturday noon.
4. **Ch IV**: Forsyth (Eton friend) on stairs of Cecil; was at Mrs. Talmage Eglinton's suite. Lunch at Strand restaurant. Forsyth reports family deaths. Sybil lives at Beaumanoir House, engaged to Forsyth. Duke offers Forsyth secretaryship (800/yr, dower-house). Mrs. Talmage Eglinton's landau: invitation to tea Saturday at the Cecil; Duke refuses; decides to be a man, not a cur. Duke to Prior's Tarrant.
5. **Ch V**: Sunday at Prior's Tarrant; Duke's fears (Ziegler, Forsyth's risk); Forsyth letter (saw Shermans at General's; engaged to Sybil). Church; vicar's lunch. Jennings lassoed in park. Night in state bedroom: charcoal brazier fumes down chimney ("Charcoal! Ziegler!").
6. **Ch VI**: Tea at 140 Grosvenor Gardens. Sybil, Leonie, Mrs. Sherman, Mrs. Sadgrove. Mrs. Talmage Eglinton calls; General returns: witnessed her landau knocking down a man in Buckingham Palace Road (the Duke). Duke visits; plaster on wrist. Duke probes about Senator's bonds: "dangerous mission." General: "His Grace knows something."
7. **Ch VII**: Forsyth's John Street chambers; Duke hides there. Marker at door as bogus chemist's messenger. Forsyth sends Duke to bedroom; goes to club for an hour. Returns: door forced with jemmy; Duke gone; two men on stairs (clergyman, tweed man).
8. **Ch VIII**: Beaumanoir House white drawing-room. "Inspector Chantrey, CID" (fake clergyman) visits Sybil at night; Duke arrives, rebukes him. Sybil overhears; Duke takes both to smoking room. At 3 a.m. Sybil hears a saw; finds Duke's door panel cut with watch-spring saw. Sybil rouses men; tweed man holds Sybil, pulls pistol; Duke disarms him ("Give me that pistol"); sends him out.
9. **Ch IX**: General at Beaumanoir House 9 a.m.; plan: move Duke to Prior's Tarrant with party (Shermans, Sadgroves, Sybil, Forsyth). Duke reluctant (charcoal). General surveils via apple-woman under railings; Steptoe sent to offer sovereign; apple-woman meets clergyman in Air Street. General visits Scotland Yard: no "Inspector Chantrey."
10. **Ch X**: General with Mrs. Sadgrove; Azimoolah ("Allah be praised! The black tribe walks again!"). Luncheon; invitations. Visit to Mrs. Talmage Eglinton at Cecil; General notes split suite (door blocked by writing-table). Azimoolah disguised as Thakore of Bhurtnagur creates uproar in Ziegler's suite; General extracts him. Mrs. T.E. asks: "When does the Duke himself go into the country?" General: "To-night, by the 8.45 from St. Pancras. Alec Forsyth goes down with him."
11. **Ch XI**: Night at Prior's Tarrant; General waits; Azimoolah reports painters in cart (dog-cart) and "red lamp" signal from French maid's window. Brougham returns empty; Forsyth arrives with telegram (forgery) claiming Sybil's distress. Train 8.45 derailed between St. Albans and Harpenden; a timber barrier. General's theory: Mrs. T.E. = Ziegler's gang. Terrace struggle: General seizes Azimoolah by mistake; Forsyth: "That's your own man, Azimoolah."
12. **Ch XII**: Duke alone in carriage (reserved; locked). Stops at Kentish Town, Hendon, Mill Hill, Elstree. Man's boot under seat = Marker. Duke pulls Marker out. Marker insists he's a stranger; ticket shown. At Radlett, Marker escapes; Duke reports; guard. Train stops on gradient: derailment; obstruction of baulks; Duke flees into wood (whistle signals, watchers). Escapes along ride.
13. **Ch XIII**: Keeper Mayne's cottage (Sir Claude Asprey's coverts; Duke shot first pheasant here at 13). Mayne: "It isn't a fortnight since his Grace your uncle and your cousin were killed." Tall American in blue suit "Colonel Anstruther Walcot" arrives; Duke claims debt to Walcot to explain flight; escapes out window of spare room onto woodshed roof. Duke walks to Prior's Tarrant; Azimoolah follows, Duke attacks him at terrace steps.
14. **Ch XIV**: General lets Azimoolah go; Duke goes to bed guarded by Forsyth. Breakfast: Duke mentions Mrs. T.E. accepted invitation. General fears for Sybil (she's the rival). Anonymous note to Mrs. Sadgrove: "There is danger from Ziegler" — scented like Mrs. T.E.'s letters. General suspects Mrs. T.E. Sybil's counsel: "Too many women" - Sybil: "you ain't one of 'em." Sybil identifies Mrs. T.E. as the ringleader.
15. **Ch XV**: Mrs. T.E. installed (two days); Sybil her constant companion. Sybil tells her General going to bearding Ziegler (ruse). Mrs. T.E. headache; leaves. Red lamp; woman leaves window; Azimoolah tracks her to park wall; dog-cart with three figures; Senalban road (St. Albans). Duke and General break headache cure. General's Ziegler visit; Duke confesses to General. Forsyth goes to Ziegler (letter from Duke promising, sent by Ziegler's agent): Ziegler's letter requests obedience.
16. **Ch XVI**: Mrs. T.E. goes to London by station brougham (Forsyth escorts); Bond Street shop. Forsyth to Cecil: Ziegler suite; Benzon ("Leopold Benzon, Mr. Ziegler's private secretary"). Ziegler interview: Forsyth denies Duke's disclosures; gets sealed packet for Duke. Mrs. T.E. in hallway (lies about jewelry). Kettner's lunch: Forsyth: "I am very far from being indifferent to you, Mrs. Talmage Eglinton."
17. **Ch XVII**: Morning: Duke missing from Prior's Tarrant. Room search: bed slept in, cold toilet, window smoking room unbolted. Azimoolah found: Duke left by wicket gate; walked to Tring; train 7.30 to Bletchley; North-of-England express. Mrs. T.E. enters; General: "Our host is all right—gone away." Mrs. T.E. pleased.
18. **Ch XVIII**: Senator Sherman on *Campania* at Liverpool. Duke (Beaumanoir) meets him; Senator suspects confidence man. Corridor express to Tarrant; Duke hiding pistol. Senator sees Duke's guard. Duke introduced to Mrs. T.E. (Senator notices her as Cora Lestrade, from Sing-Sing). Safe in muniment room, bonds locked (Duke's new safe).
19. **Ch XIX**: Midnight smoking-room; Senator and General on Cora Lestrade. Forsyth disguises as Duke (make-up); letter from Ziegler telling Duke to unbolt crypt door. Forsyth goes to crypt; swaps dummy bundle (tissue paper) for bonds; Ziegler examines; begs for bogus bonds back; Forsyth refuses and sends him away.
20. **Ch XX**: Duke alone in muniment room with revolver, waiting. Ziegler and Rosa approach; Rosa opens window; Benzon climbs in; Duke turns on light, grabs Ziegler. Senator, General, Forsyth, Sybil arrive. Azimoolah chokes Benzon; Lestrade wig removed (purple stain). Senator: "Cora Lestrade." General: Forsyth got the dummy; Cora spared Forsyth due to attachment; Benzon escapes through window. Cora pale, leaves at dawn; butler's tip.
21. **Ch XXI**: Bonds reach Bank of England. Duke confesses to Senator; Senator: "honor of your house... mixed with that of mine." Duke asks to speak with Leonie. Six months later: Forsyth (agent of ducal estates) married Sybil in September; Duke and Duchess away in Egypt; Cora Lestrade (as Countess Poniatowski) stabbed to death on Vienna train; Benzon arrested (in priest's dress). General's intuition praised.
